title: Long-term observation of the influence of the individual diagnostic and therapeutic treatment regimen on the outcome of head and neck tumors
summary:
It is assumed that the selection of examination and treatment methods for patients with tumors in the head and neck area has a major influence on how the disease develops in the long term. Thanks to modern medical advances, more people can survive today and suffer less from the consequences of the disease or treatment. In addition, their quality of life can be significantly improved. The focus is on the question: Is there an advantage if the treatment is individually tailored to each individual patient – i.e. depending on the type of tumor and personal situation? This is particularly evident in patients who are being treated entirely at the Clinic for Oral and Maxillofacial Plastic Surgery at Frankfurt University Hospital. 
In contrast to previous studies, the new study is intended to observe a larger number of patients over a significantly longer period of time (ideally up to 15 years). The aim is to provide a more accurate picture of the long-term impact of different treatment pathways. The aim of the study is to show that individually tailored treatment can help patients remain tumor-free in the long term, have fewer health problems and can lead a better life overall.
conditions: Head and Neck Tumors (Squamous Cell Carcinoma)

interventions.name: Patients with tumors in the head and neck area and surgical therapeutic approach, respectively resection of tumor, and, if indicated neck dissection and/or adjuvant radio(chemo) therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Localization of the primary tumor: head and neck area
- Surgical therapeutic procedure
Exclusion criteria:
- Primal therapy of the tumor in question not at the trial center
